facts.meaning: Local stored promise records the ballot against which accept handlers validate; it does not alone establish a read quorum or Accept phase.
facts.validity_context: Current instance with backend promise retained across crash recovery; changed by accepted Prepare or local leadership start.
facts.recovery: Build reads promise and starts Recover when present.

facts.meaning: Leader per-node support slot records an accepted index for its leader ballot; follower acknowledgments describe stored accepted length, not buffered length.
facts.validity_context: LeaderState reset for new local leadership; same-ballot messages update per-node indexes.
facts.durability: Leader aggregation volatile; node accepted history retained by backend.

facts.meaning: The stored decided boundary is the local marker used to classify entries as decided; leader advancement checks write quorum and followers receive the boundary from sync or ordered decision messages.
facts.validity_context: Current stored history, including StopSign if decided.
facts.recovery: Recovered from backend, carried in promises and synchronization.

facts.meaning: A stored snapshot object is paired with the local compacted index and returned as the representation of that prefix. Its contents are produced through Snapshot::create/merge or replacement by a complete snapshot; matching the decided prefix is the responsibility under investigation, not assumed here.
facts.validity_context: Current backend snapshot and cached compacted bound after successful snapshot or sync; delta inputs are relative to the peer decided boundary reported in Prepare/Promise.
facts.durability: Stored through atomic storage operation group; MemoryStorage is volatile.
facts.recovery: load_cache restores compacted bound; read fetches snapshot; synchronization may replace or merge it.

In-repository async invocation and completion ownership requires source trace; not externalized by caller-driven transport.
Sequence messages dispatch directly whereas heartbeat replies check config_id; legal cross-instance transport routing contract remains to be established.
Can buffer before leader known; follower sync visibly forwards ordinary proposals only. Need trace caller progress obligations and all consumers.

formation.explanation: A proposal is buffered, forwarded, or appended by the role/phase owner. Leader prepare collects distinct per-pid promises for the configured read quorum, selects highest accepted round then length and maximum decided boundary, synchronizes that history, appends pending work, and sends AcceptSync. Subsequent accepted batches go to promised followers. Followers persist synchronized or appended history before Accepted; the leader counts per-pid indexes for a write quorum and persists/sends the decided boundary. Read APIs expose decided entries or the snapshot representation; application execution is separate.

context.explanation: BLE heartbeat rounds and manual attempts propose ballots, but SequencePaxos requires a ballot above its promise and former leader state. The new leader resets aggregation and persists its promise; a follower accepts higher Prepare, or same ballot only after recovery, flushing old buffered accepts before reporting its accepted history. A higher promise rejects old accepts and reports NotAccepted. Matching ballot plus phase and sequence/session checks protect follower append/decision processing; gaps trigger recovery. Crash recovery retains the promise/history but enters Recover and disables retaining leadership at the same own ballot.

connection.explanation: Authority acquisition does not discard prior accepted or decided history: promises carry accepted round/length and decision boundary; preparation selects history before accepting new proposals. AcceptSync transfers a suffix or a complete/delta decided snapshot, with session reset for later ordered accepts. Old-ballot replies cannot count in a new LeaderState. Same-ballot recovery re-promises and resynchronizes; existing accepted support refers to that ballot history. Buffered proposals survive preparation and are incorporated by a new leader or forwarded after follower sync unless a StopSign is present. Decided StopSign seals the configuration and caller starts new instances; configuration routing premises remain open. Snapshot content reconstruction is therefore a supporting storage responsibility directly consumed by A1 formation and A2 accepted-round transition.
